chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Abdillah, from Musa ibn Sa'id, from Abdullah ibn Qasim al-Hadrami, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, made Ali (peace be upon him) a sign between Him and His creation. There is no sign between them and Him other than him. So whoever follows him is a believer, and whoever denies him is a disbeliever, and whoever doubts in him is a polytheist.
ai.seo_question: What is the theological status of Imam Ali (a.s.) as an intermediary between Allah and humanity?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) elucidates the cosmological status of Imam Ali (a.s.) as the unique role as the sole *'alam* (sign/intermediary) between Allah and creation, establishing a direct correlation between one's stance toward him and the fundamental categories of faith. This narration underscores the Shia doctrine of *Wilayat al-Ammah*, where allegiance to the Imam is not merely a political act but the definitive criterion for distinguishing between *Iman* (belief), *Kufr* (disbelief), and *Shirk* (polytheism).

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 11.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) narrates that Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) said, “The Almighty Allah has made Ali (a.s.) a sign in His creation. There is no sign between Allah and His creatures  except  Ali  (a.s.).  Whoever  obeys  him  will  be considered a believer, his deniers are infidels and those who doubt in him are polytheists.”
